votes.plain_language: Official question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended. H.R. 3978: Nuclear REFUEL (Recycling Efficient Fuels Utilizing Expedited Licensing) Act. Result: Passed.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — Ratepayer Protection Act (H R 9340)
votes.plain_language: This bill tells state utility regulators to consider making very large power users, such as data centers using 100 megawatts or more, pay the full extra cost of grid upgrades built to serve them. A two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Passage — Protecting Domestic Mining Act (H R 1501)
votes.plain_language: This bill puts mining infrastructure projects into the FAST Act's faster environmental-review process and blocks a proposed rule that would have limited which mining projects qualify. A Yea passes it. A Nay votes no.

votes.question: On Passage — HEATS Act (H R 5587)
votes.plain_language: This bill exempts certain geothermal activities on state and private lands (except Indian lands) from drilling permit requirements as well as environmental and historic preservation review requirements. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Passage — Reliable Federal Infrastructure Act (H R 4690)
votes.plain_language: This bill repeals certain energy efficiency performance standards for new federal buildings and federal buildings undergoing major renovations. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Recommit — Reliable Federal Infrastructure Act (H R 4690)
votes.plain_language: H.R. 4690 (Reliable Federal Infrastructure Act) repeals certain energy efficiency performance standards for new federal buildings and federal buildings undergoing major renovations. A motion to recommit is the minority's last formal chance to send a bill back to committee before the passage vote. A Yea supports sending it back; a Nay keeps it on the floor for the passage vote.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass — To require the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission to extend the time period during which licensees are required to commence construction of certain hydropower projects (S 1020)
votes.bill_title: A bill to require the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission to extend the time period during which licensees are required to commence construction of certain hydropower projects.
votes.plain_language: This bill authorizes the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission to extend construction deadlines for hydropower projects that were issued a license before March 13, 2020. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Passage — Homeowner Energy Freedom Act (H R 4758)
votes.plain_language: This bill repeals three Department of Energy programs: high-efficiency electric home rebates for certain low- or moderate-income households, state-based home energy efficiency contractor training grants, and assistance for states and localities to adopt specified building energy codes. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

posts.text:
🚨Attention! To foster a more productive and engaging social media environment, I am leaving X and moving over to Bluesky. To remain up-to-date on how I am working for you in Congress, please follow me on Bluesky, Facebook, and Instagram.

As always, my office remains open to assist you. If you or someone you know need assistance with a federal agency, please do not hesitate to contact my office at (805) 379-1779. I’m here to help!

Every year, I have the privilege of nominating students to represent our district at one of the five prestigious service academies in the nation.

Tomorrow, on Wednesday, June 4, my office will be hosting a virtual information night for students in California's 26th Congressional District to learn more about attending a U.S. Service Academy and the Congressional nomination process. Parents are welcome to attend too!

To learn more and RSVP, click here ⤵️
https://t.co/zcsCb3kVUu

The Trump Administration hailed DOGE as the solution to eliminating waste, fraud, and abuse, with Elon Musk promising to slash $2 trillion in government spending.

Now, Elon is walking away claiming he cut $150 billion – just 7.5% of what he promised – with no proof to back it up. Meanwhile, he burned through $135 billion in taxpayer dollars doing it.

If anyone’s a fraud, it’s Elon Musk. And if we’re talking about abuse of power, Musk is the poster child – making false claims, wasting billions, and walking away with zero accountability.

If the Trump Administration really wants to stop fraud, they need to start by addressing their own failures first.

Oh, and by the way: Musk continues to pocket money from government contracts that total $8 million a day.
https://t.co/87HS1e1zwf

The Trump Administration’s decision to revoke humanitarian protections for a four-year-old girl in Bakersfield is heartbreaking and unconscionable.
 
Two years ago, Sofia legally came to the U.S. so she could receive critical, around-the-clock care for a rare and life-threatening condition. Thanks to treatment at Children’s Hospital Los Angeles, she’s been able to survive. But now, her family is facing deportation and putting her life in immediate danger.
 
Revoking Sofia’s legal status in the U.S. and denying her access to medical care is a cruel and inhumane act that violates our most basic values.
 
I’m calling on the Trump Administration to reverse its decision and allow Sofia and her family to stay in the U.S. on humanitarian grounds. Her life depends on it.
https://t.co/otAMcO8j4d

“Though the debt we owe them can never be repaid, we must strive every day to live up to the principles they defended.”

Today and every day, we honor our fallen and recommit ourselves to the enduring values of freedom and justice they stood for, and to protecting our democracy and American way of life they gave their lives to uphold.

Their sacrifice calls on us to come together as a nation, to support our veterans and their families, and to carry forward their legacy with gratitude and resolve.

For over 29 hours, @HouseDemocrats stood united against the GOP's tax scam. I joined my colleagues in the Rules Committee to call out the outrageous and shameful Medicaid cuts in this bill. Over 265,000 people in #VenturaCounty rely on Medicaid, and I won’t stop fighting to protect their care.

As the House Rules Committee enters its 17th hour of considering one of the largest Republican rip-offs and redistributions of wealth, House Republicans are pushing a dangerous bill that would strip health care from nearly 14 million Americans and slash $300 billion from food assistance programs that 42 million people rely on – all to pay for tax breaks for billionaires. They called the meeting at 1:00 AM, hoping the American people wouldn’t notice.

But @HouseDemocrats are still here. We’ve filed 537 amendments to defend the programs working families depend on. We’re fighting back, and we are not backing down.

https://t.co/MvVKJNMExy

I am deeply saddened by the passing of my colleague and dear friend, Congressman Gerry Connolly.

A true public servant, Gerry spent every day working to improve the lives of all Americans and represented the very best of us in Congress.

For decades, he was a steadfast advocate for his constituents in Northern Virginia. He will be remembered for his leadership, his fierce commitment to America’s federal workers, and his unwavering dedication to good governance and transparency.

Gerry was a friend to all who knew him. He extended kindness to colleagues, constituents, staff, and even strangers throughout his time in Congress.

It was an honor to serve alongside him. His remarkable service, his unique and unmistakable voice, and his unfailing friendship will be deeply missed.

Gerry’s legacy lives on in the countless lives he touched. My heart is with his family, his staff, his friends, and everyone who had the privilege of serving with him as we grieve this tremendous loss.

Members of Congress have both the right and the responsibility to conduct oversight.

The bogus charges brought against @RepLaMonica are nothing more than political theater. This is a blatant attempt by the Trump Administration to distract, intimidate, and interfere with Congress’ constitutional duty to check the power of the Executive Branch.

Every time this administration is held responsible for its most egregious overreaches of power, it lashes out to silence critics and deflect from its own unlawful behavior.

I join House Democrats in standing with Congresswoman McIver. We will not be intimidated. We will continue to hold this administration accountable for its unlawful and unconstitutional actions.
https://t.co/RJP28dFYYj

This #ArmedForcesDay, we recognize the brave individuals who serve our nation in uniform, both here at home and abroad. Our servicemembers and their families are the heart and soul of America’s defense.

Words are not enough to express our country's gratitude to those who have answered the call to serve — and I will never stop fighting for them.

I would especially like to recognize the servicemembers, reservists, and their families at Naval Base Ventura County and the 146th Airlift Wing at Channel Islands Air National Guard Station, as well as those serving in the U.S. Coast Guard. I join a grateful nation in thanking you for your service and sacrifice.

During #NationalPoliceWeek, law enforcement officers from across the country descend on Washington, DC to honor the fallen and recognize the service of our nation’s heroes. Alongside them, first responders, including paramedics, nurses, and medical personnel, provide critical on-the-ground support for the week’s ceremonies and events.

This year, #VenturaCounty’s own Dave Conahey, a dedicated nurse and National Disaster Medical System (NDMS) responder from #Moorpark, was among them. Dave has deployed across the country to support communities and health systems in the wake of disasters, answering the call wherever and whenever he’s needed.

Earlier this week, I had the opportunity to meet with Dave and other first responders who work tirelessly behind the scenes to support our law enforcement officers and help our nation in times of crisis.

Every day, law enforcement officers throughout Ventura County, the Conejo Valley, and across the country put themselves in harm’s way to keep our communities safe.

This #NationalPoliceWeek, and every week, we recognize their service, their sacrifice, and their unwavering commitment to the people they serve.
Photo Credit: Oxnard Police Department
https://t.co/ENlBpVBiid
https://t.co/9bPjfuwOps

Earlier this week, the Oxnard Police Department held its 26th Annual Police Memorial Ceremony to honor the memory of seven fallen officers who made the ultimate sacrifice in the line of duty.

As we reflect on their bravery, we are reminded of the profound courage and commitment of law enforcement officers here in #VenturaCounty and across the country.

On #PeaceOfficersMemorialDay, and every day, we honor their service and express our deepest gratitude for their selfless dedication to protecting and serving our communities.

Donald Trump plans to accept a $400 million luxury plane from the Qatari royal family, and he wants to keep it after leaving office.

This isn’t a gift. It’s corruption. It’s unconstitutional. And it’s a direct threat to our national security.

And make no mistake about it, this jet isn’t free. Taxpayers would be on the hook for hundreds of millions just to make it usable for the president.

The Emoluments Clause is clear: no president can accept gifts from foreign governments without Congress’ approval. Trump knows that, and he’s doing it anyway.

Meanwhile, he’s telling working families their kids should settle for “two dolls” because his tariffs are driving up prices. While Americans pay more, Trump is taking a luxury jet and sending them the bill. #GrifterInChief
https://t.co/jJgEU2N3bB

In the United States, 1 in 5 adults experience mental health challenges. That’s why we must recommit to ending the stigma and raising awareness about the resources available to those who are struggling.

The 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline is available 24/7 by call, text, or chat at https://t.co/O9B106Bqwv. Remember: You are not alone, and it’s always okay to ask for help.

Together, we can turn struggle into strength, silence into change, and stories into hope. #MentalHealthAwarenessMonth

Happy Mother’s Day to all the mothers and mother figures in our lives!

As a mother and grandmother, I know the job is far from easy, but the journey of motherhood is deeply rewarding.

Today, we celebrate the incredible women who have guided us, inspired us, and helped us reach our fullest potential. We are forever grateful for their strength, their sacrifices, and, most of all, their love.

Small businesses are the backbone of our economy, especially here in #VenturaCounty and the Conejo Valley, where over 22,000 small businesses drive innovation, create jobs, and power our region.

But many small businesses are being squeezed by the fallout from President Trump’s reckless trade war. Nearly 90% rely on imported goods and materials, but unlike big corporations, they don’t have global logistics teams or legal departments to help them overcome these challenges that can be detrimental to their survival. They are being left to deal with this tariff mess on their own, and it’s hurting workers, families, and our local economy.

In Congress, I am fighting for trade policies that put small businesses and working families first. #SmallBusinessWeek #SmallBusinessSaturday

I recently joined First 5 Ventura for their Take 5 🖐 and Read to Kids! campaign to encourage families to talk, read, and sing with young children. Together, we’re raising awareness about the critical importance of early childhood language and literacy development.

Every child deserves the chance to dream big. When we invest in early literacy, we’re not just reading stories – we’re helping build a brighter future for them.

financial_disclosures.caption: Official House financial disclosure filings from the Clerk of the House. A filing lists assets, income, liabilities, and trades the member reported; it is not proof of a conflict or of wrongdoing. Dollar ranges and asset names are in the PDF. This page links to the Clerk's copies and does not score anyone.

funding.heading: Disclosed campaign receipts
funding.detail: Federal cards show the principal campaign committee and OpenFEC totals for one two-year cycle, plus itemized Schedule A contributors. House uses 2026. Senate uses the cycle of the next election (2026, 2028, or 2030). This is not career fundraising and does not include Schedule E outside spending. Governors do not get a federal contribution list.

town_halls.note: There is no national town-hall dataset. Dates are not estimated.

disclosure_note: Disclosed contributions only; donors behind groups that do not report their own donors are not in this feed.
vote_scope: This is not a full career record. The cache is the latest 40 House rolls (2026, rolls 275-314) and 40 Senate votes (119th Congress, session 2, votes 217-256).
